annotations.text:
A — INSTRUMENT (dark)

Direct descendant of the AGP report prototype: same near-black stage, Mulish, blue accent, amber highlight. Cards are dense instrument panels; each carries a real figure motif.

For: continuity with the AGP/Microsetta visual family, and it makes the data feel live.
Against: dark sites are harder for a people-heavy, undergrad-facing site; figures exported from R/Python are almost all white-background and will need re-rendering to sit on it.

B — FIELD PLATE (warm)

Natural-history publication: cream paper, Instrument Serif masthead, the three projects as numbered plates with captions under each illustration.

For: the tree-of-life subject matter earns it, it reads as scholarly rather than startup, and existing white-background figures drop straight in.
Against: least like the AGP prototype; serif display can read old-fashioned, and the plate frame gets crowded once real figures replace the motifs.

C — SPECIMEN GRID (stark)

Utilitarian: hairline grid, IBM Plex Mono labels, three full-height columns that invert to solid ink on hover. No illustration — numbers and structure carry it.

For: the MMC audit story is fundamentally about record-keeping, and this looks like a catalogue; also the cheapest to extend to People and Publications tables.
Against: coldest of the three, and least distinctive as a memory — it borrows a common look.

SHARED ACROSS ALL THREE (decisions already locked in the handoff)

· Header lists all three institutions — UC San Diego, Northwestern, Johns Hopkins.
· A real front page: the three project cards ARE the primary navigation, with a pronounced hover.
· Nav reorganised around the three projects; the old Research page distributes into GMToL and HMToL.
· Publications is one entry: DeGregori et al. 2024, Biological Reviews, doi 10.1111/brv.13161.

STILL OPEN — needs your call before Phase 2
· What lands under GMToL vs HMToL vs MMC, and where People and Publications sit relative to them.
· Every number on these cards is from the legacy site copy (17,000 samples / 828 host species / 170 studies / 79 countries / 2,300 papers / 10.8% reusable). The coverage bars in C are illustrative — the 62% and 41% are placeholders, not measured.
· HMToL has no legacy page of its own, so its blurb here is written from the handoff's framing as the human-focused successor. Check the wording.
